## 固定收益市場主論述

美國勞動需求維持韌性、服務業活動轉強，加上科技股強勁上漲，影響蓋過油價再度下跌，美債殖利率6月30日全線走高。2年期殖利率上升6.8個基點至4.175%，5年期上升8.4個基點至4.227%，10年期上升9個基點至4.466%，30年期則上升8.8個基點至4.953%。這波走勢逆轉前一週大部分債券漲幅，從政策敏感的短端到長債，殖利率全面收高。

本輪賣壓主要由實質利率驅動。10年期實質殖利率上升7.8個基點至2.226%，10年期損益兩平通膨率卻僅增加1.2個基點至2.24%，顯示投資人上調的是經濟承受限制性政策的能力，而非對累積通膨衝擊的預期。5月職缺增至759萬個，6月消費者信心小幅改善，達拉斯聯準銀行的德州服務業調查亦顯示營收與就業成長加快。房價轉弱、消費者對勞動市場的看法惡化，使整體訊號並非一面倒強勁，但不足以扭轉方向。

能源價格下跌抑制通膨補償升幅。儘管美國與伊朗談判仍未解決，交易員持續反映荷莫茲海峽有序恢復通行的情境，WTI下跌1.77%至$69.50，布蘭特原油下跌0.31%至$72.92；兩項基準油價全月跌幅均超過20%。油價回落降低未來整體物價受衝擊的風險，但德州調查顯示，服務業者仍面臨投入與工資成本大幅上升。市場因而清楚區分了交易市場能源價格下降，以及國內需求和成本壓力持續存在這兩項訊號。

股市表現進一步強化這項區別。標普500指數上漲0.79%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.68%，費城半導體指數大漲3.92%，晶片股並創下歷來最佳季度表現；VIX下跌6.8%至16.45。風險偏好強勁，加上市場對AI相關獲利抱持信心，削弱公債需求；與此同時，科技業擴建背後的槓桿、債務到期結構及資本密集程度也日益受到關注。

美國以外市場呈現不同走勢。油價下跌使歐洲立場更明顯轉向鴿派，法國與德國通膨低於預期，多名歐洲央行官員也表示，立即再度升息的理由已經減弱。日本則朝相反方向發展：2年期公債標售需求強勁，但日圓疲弱、財政擴張，以及政治力量要求日本央行審慎升息，擴大政策敏感短債與超長債的分歧，30年期殖利率上升11個基點。

整體信用市場仍然暢通，但內部的區別定價日益鮮明。新興市場國際債上半年發行額創下$4,500億紀錄，利差則收窄至2007年以來最低，日本借款人的外幣發行額也創季度新高。然而，Sable Offshore即使縮減貸款規模，仍難以完成一筆利率15%的融資；中國則著手勸阻負債沉重的地方政府融資平台從事昂貴的境外借款。當日訊息並非融資已變得稀缺，而是市場行情雖然熱絡，資金更願意獎勵規模及被視為品質較佳的借款人，對急迫再融資、現金流不確定及政策風險則索取高昂代價。

## 美國數據推升實質殖利率

5月職缺與勞動力流動調查，是對此前債券漲勢最明確的全國性挑戰。職缺增至759萬個，略高於修正後的4月水準，也高於市場預期。單憑職缺增加尚不能證明非農就業成長正在加速，但數據顯示勞動需求並未弱到足以迫使聯準會偏離6月會議採取的抗通膨立場。

汽油價格下降抵銷部分就業疑慮，6月消費者信心也小幅上升，但細項不如整體指標一致強勁。消費者對勞動市場的評價轉差，且預期未來數月改善有限。對利率而言，重要之處在於這組數據尚不足以引發成長恐慌：家庭信心改善，勞動市場展望僅略微轉弱，聯準會仍有空間等待更完整的就業報告。

達拉斯聯準銀行的德州服務業調查擴大了活動回溫的證據。6月營收指數由5.0升至9.8，就業指數由-3.2躍升至8.1，工時指數則由-0.5升至3.6。一般商業活動指數由-7.7回到正值2.9，公司展望指數也由-5.4改善至6.1。企業對未來6個月同樣樂觀，預期營收指數為33.3，未來一般商業活動指數為17.2。

這項改善伴隨令人不安的成本組合。投入價格指數由29.7升至36.5，工資與福利指數由6.2升至15.3，銷售價格指數也由5.0升至7.7。這份調查延續前一日德州製造業報告的雙面訊號：區域需求與招聘正在轉強，供應鏈中的成本壓力也同步升高。因此，市場有理由推升實質殖利率，卻不能把原油下跌視為通膨問題的完整解方。

房市形成部分制衡。FHFA房價指數4月較3月下跌0.1%，年增率放緩至2%；3月月增幅則由0.1%上修至0.2%。各地區表現顯示全國動能有限，單月變動介於山區下跌0.8%與新英格蘭上漲1%之間，年增率則從太平洋區的0.2%到東北中部區的4.4%不等。房價成長放慢，可減輕一項住房成本與抵押品價值壓力，但數據反映的是4月情況，無法壓過時間較近的勞動與服務業證據。

由於賣壓遍及整條曲線，殖利率曲線僅小幅陡峭化。2年與10年期利差擴大2.2個基點至29.1個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大2個基點至77.8個基點。然而，整個6月的曲線仍顯著趨平：2年期殖利率上升17個基點，10年期僅上升2.9個基點，30年期更下降2.1個基點。這項月度走勢反映聯準會轉趨鷹派與油價崩跌，前者推高短期政策利率的預期路徑，後者則降低較長期通膨補償。

週二10年期實質殖利率升至2.226%，較一個月前高19.3個基點；同期10年期損益兩平通膨率則下降16.4個基點。這項分歧正是6月調整的核心：投資人移除了大部分戰事相關通膨溢價，卻未重新轉向寬鬆敘事。就業證據轉強、消費維持韌性，以及AI建設的資本需求，共同使實質折現率維持高檔。

季末美債交易量異常龐大。FINRA記錄的面額交易額達$1.864兆，較前一交易日增加59.3%，共計527,867筆。名目附息債交易額增加60.9%至$1.388兆；剩餘期限不超過2年的附息債交易額增加68.6%至$3,383億，2年以上至3年期區間更增加逾一倍，達$2,002億。TIPS交易額增加113.5%至$681億。這些數據反映雙向交易，而非投資人的淨方向，但足以說明本輪賣壓發生在季末廣泛調整資產負債表與投資組合之際，並非清淡市場中的價格跳動。

短端同時吸收了$800億的42天期國庫券標售，最高得標利率為3.655%，投標倍數2.71倍。間接投標人獲配已接受競爭性投標的69.01%，直接投標人占4.96%，一級交易商占26.03%。國庫券於7月2日交割、8月13日到期，顯示跨越季末與美國獨立紀念日融資期間的現金需求充足；但由於沒有發行前交易水準可供比較，無法判斷標售是否出現尾差或得標利率低於當時市場水準。

跨資產交易也支持實質殖利率主導走勢的解讀。Nasdaq 100與半導體指數表現優於大盤，美元指數幾乎持平於101.19，黃金在$4,023附近變動不大。廣泛掛牌交易的債券基金走弱，其中投資級債券基金LQD下跌0.57%，新興市場債券基金EMB下跌0.39%，高收益債券基金僅小幅下滑。這些價格走勢較符合公債殖利率上升與股票風險偏好強勁的環境，而非企業償債能力普遍惡化。

## 歐洲通膨降溫，升息急迫性降低

各國通膨報告使歐洲的討論重點改變：問題不再是歐洲央行是否必須在6月升息後迅速追加緊縮，而是能否等待第二輪效應的證據。德國6月通膨率由2.7%降至2.4%，低於2.5%的預測中位數；法國通膨率由2.8%降至2%，降幅遠大於市場預期的2.3%；義大利通膨也意外放緩至3.1%。西班牙的3.6%仍是主要大型經濟體中的例外。

法國細項強化了改善並非僅來自燃料的判斷。服務通膨由2.1%降至1.8%，商品價格繼5月年減0.6%後，年減幅擴大至0.9%。家庭需求並未崩落：消費支出在4月下降0.5%後，5月增加0.5%，高於預期的0.3%。德國統計機關則把通膨連續第二個月放緩，主要歸因於能源成本趨於溫和。

德國勞動市場仍然低迷。經季節調整後的失業人數6月僅減少1,000人；未經調整的失業人數減少15,000人至293.6萬人，但仍比一年前多22,000人，失業率則由6.3%降至6.2%。BA-X勞動需求指數持平於103，最新估計的社會保險就業人數較一年前減少71,000人。通膨降溫之際，勞動市場並未提供進一步大力緊縮的充分理由。

歐洲央行官員並未宣告能源衝擊已經結束，但支持7月立即升息的陣營有所鬆動。首席經濟學家Philip Lane關注連續4個月能源成本上升，可能如何傳導至食品與服務價格，並強調這類間接效應需要時間才會顯現。荷蘭央行總裁Olaf Sleijpen同樣表示，完整的傳導過程仍有不確定性，未來工資要求將是重要考驗；兩人均未承諾再次升息。

通常立場較鷹派的比利時央行總裁Pierre Wunsch表示，可能仍有必要再次升息，但理由已不如6月時有力。若新數據支持緊縮，他贊成不要過度拖延，卻明確拒絕承諾7月行動。芬蘭央行總裁Olli Rehn將能源衝擊形容為停滯性通膨，但表示尚未看到重大的第二輪效應，並認為通膨預期仍受控制。

鴿派官員則更清楚列出暫停升息的條件。斯洛維尼亞央行的Primoz Dolenc表示，如果油氣價格維持低檔、市場波動沒有擴散，且第二輪效應未出現，7月可以不升息。依目前證據，他認為等到9月再行動較為適當；但若地緣政治再次升溫或油價大幅上漲，升息需求可能重現。拉脫維亞央行總裁Martins Kazaks也表示，連續升息的急迫性已顯著降低，而且不再緊縮的機率並非零。

這並非否定6月的決策。Kazaks認為，近4個月能源價格居高不下，足以支持當時升息；Lane與歐洲央行總裁Christine Lagarde也主張，後續發展並未推翻該項決定。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel仍擔心能源衝擊正在經濟中持續傳導。官員的分歧在於第二次行動的時機與所需證據，而非歐洲央行是否應忽視高於目標的通膨。

英國面臨相近但對成長更敏感的問題。最終數據確認，第1季實質GDP成長0.6%，此前2025年第4季增幅修正為0.1%。服務業成長0.8%，生產與營建業各成長0.2%。人均GDP較前季上升0.6%、較一年前上升0.7%，但2025年全年成長率由1.4%下修至1.3%。

家庭財務狀況弱於產出數據表面。人均實質可支配所得繼前季增加1.2%後下跌0.8%，儲蓄率由9.6%降至8.9%。排除貴金屬的基礎經常帳赤字，由前季的£182億、占GDP 2.4%，縮小至£151億、占GDP 1.9%；改善來自初次所得赤字縮小，但排除貴金屬的貿易赤字則由£25億擴大至£77億。

英格蘭銀行總裁Andrew Bailey表示，在伊朗戰事打斷通膨降溫路徑之前，經濟疲弱原本已使央行朝降息兩次的方向前進。油價從高於$110回落至低於$80，降低衝擊持久化的風險，但Bailey仍預期通膨將由2.8%升至今年稍後約3.2%。他著眼於未來兩至三年的展望及疲弱經濟：金融環境收緊為英格蘭銀行爭取了時間，但能源衝擊延後了通膨如期回到2%目標的時點。

## 日本短端吸引買盤，長端失去定錨

日本債市出現當日最明顯的曲線分歧。2年期JGB標售投標倍數達4.82倍，高於前次的3.70倍及過去12個月平均的3.74倍；標售尾差由0.02縮小至0.005，結果公布後2年期殖利率下跌。日本央行把政策利率升至31年高點後，投資人認為短端已具吸引力，政府偏好後續審慎緊縮的訊號也提供支持。

超長債走勢相反。30年期殖利率一度升至3.95%，收高11個基點至3.94%；20年期殖利率則上升9個基點至3.64%。市場擔心首相高市早苗的財政議程、要求日本央行保持審慎的政治壓力，以及日圓貶值，可能使長期通膨和政府借款失去可靠定錨。

政府投資路線圖擬在2040會計年度前，為AI、半導體等戰略產業動員逾¥370兆資金。計畫結合公私部門資源，但在政府債務已超過GDP 200%的經濟體中，其龐大規模加深財政疑慮。官方政策指引同時預料將要求適當管理貨幣政策，市場把這項措辭解讀為鼓勵日本央行審慎行動。

日圓疲弱使這套政策組合更難維持。儘管日本央行最近升息，政府今年稍早也曾干預匯市，日圓截至6月底仍貶至一美元兌162.40日圓，創1986年以來最低。日本在4月28日至5月27日期間動用¥11.73兆支撐日圓，但美日利差與海外投資資金流持續有利美元，干預效果隨之消退。財務大臣片山皋月重申當局準備在必要時採取行動，但警告力道並未明顯加強。

日圓走弱會推高進口能源與原料成本，而政治上反對日本央行快速緊縮，又限制了最直接的貨幣政策回應。這種張力說明2年期公債需求強勁，為何未能支撐長端。審慎的日本央行可以穩定政策敏感券種；但若同樣的審慎態度讓匯率貶值與通膨風險延續，超長債投資人就會要求更高補償。

新任日本央行審議委員Ayano Sato進一步加深外界對未來政策委員會偏向寬鬆的觀感。她在首次記者會上表示，通膨常態尚未穩固形成，並拒絕透露自己將如何投票；她將從7月30日至31日的會議起參與決策。高市早苗先前任命的Toichiro Asada對6月升息投下唯一反對票；Sato接替的Junko Nakagawa則曾因主張緊縮而投下反對票。Sato一人無法決定9人委員會的方向，但這次人事更替使市場更關注未來任命將如何改變委員會平衡。

日本國內買方開始回應較高的長端殖利率。明治安田生命保險計畫在截至2027年3月的會計年度買進逾¥2兆超長期JGB，是原計畫的兩倍。該公司認為目前附近的殖利率具吸引力，並預期30年期殖利率仍將低於5%至6%區間，近期上緣約在4%區間中段。這項需求可能發揮穩定作用，但財政與匯率疑慮升高之際，仍未能阻止週二超長債遭到拋售。

亞洲另一項重要活動訊號來自中國。6月官方製造業PMI由50.0升至50.3，其中生產指數為51.4，新訂單為51.2；新出口訂單由48.6回升至擴張區間的50.1。非製造業商務活動指數由50.1微升至50.2，綜合產出指數升至50.6。

然而，數據廣度不如整體指標跨過榮枯線所顯示的強勁。製造業就業指數降至48.5，小型企業PMI降至48.2，營建業指數為49.0。非製造業新訂單雖改善3點，仍處於收縮區間的48.0，投入價格指數則降至49.7。數據反映產出與出口需求正在復甦，但招聘、小型企業及營建業尚未普遍改善。

儘管如此，油價回落及穩定匯率的努力仍有利區域債券資金流。截至6月26日，外資淨買進$12億印尼公債，使6月有望創13個月來最大單月流入。印尼央行意外升息後，今年累計緊縮幅度達100個基點，10年期殖利率由6月初高點7.47%降至7.12%；印尼盾也從歷史低點反彈約2%。

印度取消公債稅負後，6月符合指數納入資格的公債獲外資買進3,980億盧比，約合$42億，創歷史新高。油價下降改善這個高度依賴進口能源經濟體的前景，印度盧比也從歷史低點回升。歐洲承認印度清算公司為合格中央交易對手，另行排除了德意志銀行、法國巴黎銀行等銀行面臨的一項障礙，降低交易印度債券與衍生性金融商品的資本和營運摩擦。

## 信用市場暢通，再融資風險仍受嚴厲定價

新興市場借款人在上半年結束前，把握信用利差極窄的有利發行環境。2026年前6個月，主權與企業發行的美元及歐元計價國際債券達到創紀錄的$4,500億，比一年前增加15%。墨西哥、沙烏地阿拉伯、南韓、波蘭、土耳其及巴西各自籌得逾$100億。

6月新興市場債相對美債的額外殖利率收窄至154個基點，為2007年以來最低。上半年新興市場美元債報酬率為2.1%，約是所引指數中美債報酬率的三倍。油價下降、美國與伊朗和解取得進展，以及全球儲蓄長期分散配置、降低對美國資產依賴，共同支撐需求，使成熟借款人得以用歷史上極低的風險溢酬發債。

日本企業的海外融資也創新高。季度外幣債發行額約達$540億，較一年前同期增加逾80%，也是自1999年有資料以來，單季總額首度突破$500億。瑞穗金融集團與三井住友金融集團合計為近$100億美元債完成定價，Panasonic也啟動另一筆美元債發行。

日圓疲弱，使日本發行人把外幣募集款項換回日圓後，能取得更多本國資金；本地利率上升則降低在國內借款的相對吸引力，海外併購亦構成外幣發債的結構性動機。因此，發行紀錄不只是利用利差收窄的機會，也反映日本企業正調整融資結構，以因應國內殖利率上升與更龐大的國際投資布局。

中國採取相反方向，試圖限制昂貴的境外再融資。據知情人士透露，國家發展和改革委員會要求部分銀行業者，避免承銷殖利率高於4%的境外人民幣債券，以及殖利率高於5%的美元債券。部分地方政府融資平台的境外再融資額度遭削減10%至20%，至少一家國有企業因而轉向成本較高的短期銀行貸款填補缺口。

相關限制針對的是境外流通債券約達$1,170億的產業。更廣泛而言，中國企業在2026年剩餘期間約有$710億境外債到期，2027年到期高峰則超過$1,300億。壓低成本的紀律可減少高票息債務累積，但當境外市場殖利率高於監管門檻時，也可能迫使較弱的發行人轉向期限更短的銀行融資，或留下更大的再融資缺口。

Sable Offshore則呈現槓桿融資市場雖大致友善，個別發行人仍可能受挫的另一面。公司宣布計畫透過股票與可轉換公司債發行籌措$4億，以償還Exxon Mobil貸款，消息公布後股價一度重挫55%。原擬發行$10億的定期貸款，在固定利率高達15%、發行價為每一美元面額97美分的條件下需求仍然有限，因此第二度縮減至$6.75億。

這筆兩年半期貸款還要求部分攤還本金，擬議可轉換公司債則提供最高6.5%的票息及30%至35%的轉換溢價。Sable先前已向Exxon支付$3,000萬，延後原訂6月26日的到期日，之後期限預計延至7月31日。其加州離岸業務重啟仍涉及訴訟，投資人因此必須同時評估近期還款壓力，以及基礎業務能否持續。這項困難屬發行人特有；其他槓桿借款人仍在收窄定價，並提前交易截止時間。

衣索比亞債務重整則引發另一類債權人爭議。代表約45%違約2024年到期票據持有人的委員會，確認已就主要條款達成初步協議，推動債券價格升至面額每一美元109.17美分，接近6個月高點。不過，該團體指控IMF處理程序不當，並認為IMF既是優先債權人，又負責評估債務減免需求，構成利益衝突。IMF表示協議符合恢復債務永續性的目標，並為其架構的一致性與透明度辯護。潛在和解有所進展，但爭議顯示債券價格回升不等於市場信任主權債務重整程序。

私人信貸資本也開始流向可能出現壓力的領域。Len Tannenbaum正為一檔新基金尋求家族辦公室支持，其家族準備投入最高$5,000萬，並以10月初完成首次募資為目標。他預期私人信貸工具的資金流出將促使利差擴大、契約條款轉向有利貸方，尤以下層中型市場最為明顯，並認為規模較小的軟體借款人未來一年將面臨再融資困難。這檔擬議基金尚未提交相關文件，也尚未決定未來的商業發展公司將採公開或私募形式。

IMF的Tobias Adrian指出，大型科技借款人也有相關弱點。他認為，相較於偏高的股票估值，舉債融資更值得憂慮，原因是超大規模科技公司正以中長期債務為實體資產與晶片提供資金，而這些資產可能在債務到期前就已過時。持續獲利可維持這種結構，但獲利一旦不如預期，期限錯配便會暴露。半導體股創下歷來最佳季度表現之際，企業與政府又承諾投入鉅額資金建設AI基礎設施，使這項警告更具現實意義。

## 新興市場政策路徑分歧

哥倫比亞做出當日幅度最大的實際政策調整，把基準利率上調75個基點至12%。這是3月以來首次升息，幅度高於受訪26名分析師中多數人的預期。7名理事中有4人支持這項決定，1人主張按兵不動，另有2人希望降息50個基點；儘管整體升幅很大，投票仍反映決策反應高度分歧。

央行援引高於目標的通膨預期及緊俏勞動市場。5月年通膨率加速至5.8%，創近兩年最快；央行調查的經濟學家預期年底將升至約6.5%，遠高於3%的目標及上下各1個百分點的容許區間。龐大財政赤字與創紀錄的最低工資調幅也加重壓力。

制度環境同樣有所改變。法院暫停財政部長必須出席政策會議的規定，移除政府過去可藉威脅杯葛會議、阻止決策的機制。保守派Abelardo de la Espriella在總統大選擊敗Iván Cepeda，也降低政治壓力持續干預央行的疑慮。選後債券與匯率均已上漲，讓決策官員有更多空間重新彰顯抗通膨職責。

南非下一步仍未落實，但政策前景更加鷹派。兩年後的平均通膨預期由3.6%升至3.9%，是一年多來首次上升，並高於央行3%的目標。前次升息已把政策利率推至7%，Goldman Sachs預期7月23日會議將一致通過再升息25個基點；遠期利率協議顯示，再升息一碼的機率為88%。

南非調查於5月18日至6月4日進行，早於美國與伊朗達成60天停火、荷莫茲海峽恢復通行及能源價格下跌，因此對其後油價反轉的反映有限。Goldman預期燃料轉便宜將在未來數月壓低通膨，央行可能在7月升息後暫停，並於2027年第2季恢復降息。當前主張緊縮的理由，是防止通膨預期根深蒂固，而非假設能源衝擊會保持先前的強度。

波蘭呈現相反結果。6月通膨率連續第三個月放緩，由3.1%降至2.5%，低於2.7%的預測中位數。茲羅提兌歐元下跌0.3%，基準公債則上漲，10年期殖利率降至3月初以來最低。當地經濟學家表示，再次升息的機率已接近零，衍生性金融商品定價也顯示最終降息的機率升高。

波蘭數據顯示，油價下跌正使區域政策路徑分化。中東衝突造成的通膨影響小於原先擔憂，6月也是數據連續第四次低於預期。央行未來幾次會議仍可能維持利率不變，但若成長或核心通膨轉弱，便可能開啟降息空間。肥料成本仍是食品價格展望的較長期風險。

紐西蘭面臨較漸進的政策正常化討論。IMF表示，紐西蘭央行應撤回寬鬆措施，並在2026年底前把目前2.25%的政策利率推向以3%左右為中心的中性水準。這項建議未指明應在下次會議或9月開始緊縮，而是以核心通膨、中期通膨預期及經濟復甦作為政策路徑的條件。IMF預期，第2季經濟收縮後，復甦將於下半年重新展開。

智利的殖利率曲線顯示，通膨改善可與財政造成的長天期風險惡化並存。1年期損益兩平通膨率全月下降逾100個基點至2.19%，低於央行3%的目標；受訪分析師與交易員中，逾40%預期披索債券殖利率將於7月下跌。市場定價顯示一年後政策利率為4.38%，低於目前的4.5%。

不過，智利政府放棄在2030年前平衡結構性預算的計畫，改以任期結束前把赤字控制在GDP的1.5%為目標，並要求取得2026年額外發行$62億債券的權限，長期殖利率因而上升。通膨降低及經濟閒置產能支撐較短期限債券，潛在供給與較弱的財政定錨則推高曲線遠端的期限溢價。

## 後續市場意義

7月1日歐洲中部夏令時間11:00公布的歐元區初值通膨，是第一項重大考驗。5月整體通膨率為3.2%，排除能源的指標為2.4%。主要國家的數據指向放緩，但彼此差異仍使歐洲央行聚焦服務、食品與工資是否出現Lane和Sleijpen所述的延遲傳導。若各類別普遍降溫，將增強7月暫停升息的理由；若排除能源後的通膨仍具黏性，再次升息仍會是選項。

美國接著將於東部時間08:15公布ADP就業，09:45公布製造業PMI終值，10:00公布ISM製造業指數與營建支出。前次ISM報告的製造業指數為54.0、價格指數82.1、就業指數48.6。訂單、招聘與價格將顯示，JOLTS及德州服務業的韌性究竟代表全國經濟再度加速，或只是少數地區數據偏強。

美國財政部將於7月1日東部時間11:30標售$720億17週期國庫券，7月7日交割、11月3日到期。這次標售緊接42天期國庫券獲市場穩健吸收之後，但交割日已跨過季末。結果將檢驗季末報表日的短期壓力消退後、且在7月2日縮短交易時段之前，需求是否仍然強勁。

因假期提前公布的美國就業報告與初領失業救濟金人數，將於7月2日東部時間08:30出爐。5月非農就業增加172,000人，失業率為4.3%，平均時薪較前月增加0.3%、較一年前增加3.4%。6月就業組成，尤其是工資，以及招聘能否擴大至防禦型產業以外，將是近期檢驗實質殖利率上升所反映聯準會緊縮傾向的最重要數據。

5月工廠訂單將於東部時間10:00公布，此前耐久財訂單初值下降4.5%。財政部接著於11:30分別標售$850億4週期與8週期國庫券，均於7月7日交割。SIFMA建議固定收益市場於東部時間14:00收盤，使就業、工廠數據、國庫券供給與部位調整集中在縮短的交易時段內。美國固定收益市場7月3日休市，紐約聯準銀行當日不公布參考利率，公開市場交易室也不操作。

日本7月2日約¥2.6兆的10年期JGB標售，將檢驗2年期標售呈現的強勁短端需求，能否延伸至核心期限。標售之際，日圓正處於40年低點，日本央行政策委員會看來更偏寬鬆，超長債也才剛歷經大幅賣壓。7月7日約¥6,000億的30年期標售，則是更直接的考驗，可觀察保險公司增加購債的計畫，能否穩定曲線中最容易受到財政擴張與長期通膨不確定性影響的區段。

能源仍是上述政策考驗的共同條件。WTI在6月下跌逾20%後，以接近$69.50作收；但卡達把杜哈談判形容為間接磋商，並淡化立即取得突破的可能性。荷莫茲海峽若持續暢通、停火得以長久維持，整體通膨緩解便可延續；若攻擊再起、海運通行受限，或和解未能正式落實，能源通膨與長端期限溢價將重新成為全球利率交易的核心。

overall_summary.headline: 美國需求展現韌性、實質利率上升，美債殖利率躍升
overall_summary.session_narrative:
6月30日美債殖利率全線上升，逆轉前一週大部分債券漲幅。2年期殖利率上升6.8個基點至4.175%，5年期上升8.4個基點至4.227%，10年期上升9個基點至4.466%，30年期則上升8.8個基點至4.953%。

走勢主要由實質利率驅動：10年期實質殖利率上升7.8個基點至2.226%，10年期損益兩平通膨率僅增加1.2個基點至2.24%。職缺增至759萬個、消費者信心小幅改善，德州服務業的營收與就業成長加快，投入及工資成本也同步上升。房價轉弱、消費者對勞動市場的看法惡化，使訊號有所保留，但未引發成長恐慌。

油價下跌抑制通膨補償，科技股領漲及波動率降低則強化風險偏好，削弱公債需求。歐洲通膨數據轉弱，降低歐洲央行立即再升息的急迫性。日本走勢分歧：2年期公債標售需求強勁，但日圓疲弱、財政擴張及要求日本央行審慎緊縮的壓力，使30年期殖利率上升11個基點。

整體信用市場維持暢通，但選擇性升高。新興市場與日本外幣債發行額創新高，Sable Offshore卻難以完成一筆利率15%的貸款；中國也著手限制負債沉重的地方政府融資平台從事昂貴的境外再融資。
overall_summary.summary: 勞動與服務業數據穩健，加上科技股領漲，推升實質殖利率並引發美債全面賣壓；油價下跌則限制通膨補償的升幅。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off across the curve on June 30 as resilient U.S. labor demand, firmer service-sector activity and a powerful technology-stock rally outweighed another decline in oil. The 2-year yield rose 6.8 basis points to 4.175%, the 5-year climbed 8.4 basis points to 4.227%, the 10-year increased 9 basis points to 4.466% and the 30-year advanced 8.8 basis points to 4.953%. The move reversed much of the preceding week’s duration rally and left yields higher from the policy-sensitive front end through the long bond.

The selloff was predominantly a real-rate move. The 10-year real yield increased 7.8 basis points to 2.226%, while the 10-year breakeven inflation rate rose only 1.2 basis points to 2.24%. That composition showed investors marking up the economy’s capacity to withstand restrictive policy more than the expected cumulative inflation impulse. May job openings reached 7.59 million, June consumer confidence edged higher and the Dallas Fed’s Texas services survey reported faster revenue and employment growth. Softer house prices and deteriorating consumer views of the labor market qualified the picture but did not overturn it.

Lower energy prices constrained the rise in inflation compensation. WTI fell 1.77% to $69.50 and Brent slipped 0.31% to $72.92 as traders continued to price an orderly reopening of the Strait of Hormuz despite unresolved U.S.-Iran negotiations. Both benchmarks were more than 20% lower over the month. The retreat reduced the prospective headline-price shock, but the Texas survey showed that service businesses were still encountering sharply higher input and wage costs. The session therefore separated cheaper traded energy from persistent domestic demand and cost pressure.

Equities reinforced that distinction. The S&P 500 rose 0.79%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.68% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 3.92%, completing a record quarter for chip shares. The VIX declined 6.8% to 16.45. Strong risk appetite and confidence in AI-related earnings reduced demand for government bonds even as concern grew about the leverage, debt maturity and capital intensity behind the technology buildout.

Outside the United States, lower oil produced a more visibly dovish shift in Europe, where French and German inflation undershot forecasts and several European Central Bank officials said the case for an immediate second increase had weakened. Japan moved in the opposite direction: strong demand at a 2-year auction contrasted with an 11-basis-point rise in the 30-year yield as yen weakness, fiscal expansion and political pressure for a cautious Bank of Japan widened the divide between policy-sensitive and super-long debt.

Credit markets remained open at the aggregate level but increasingly discriminating underneath. Emerging-market international issuance reached a first-half record of $450 billion as spreads touched their tightest level since 2007, and Japanese borrowers set a quarterly record in foreign currencies. Yet Sable Offshore struggled to place a 15% loan even after reducing its size, while China moved to discourage expensive offshore borrowing by heavily indebted local-government financing vehicles. The day’s broad message was not that financing had become scarce, but that buoyant markets were rewarding scale and perceived quality while charging heavily for urgent refinancing, uncertain cash generation and policy risk.

## U.S. Data Push Real Yields Higher

The May Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey supplied the clearest national challenge to the preceding duration rally. Available positions rose to 7.59 million, slightly above the revised April level and above expectations. The increase did not by itself establish accelerating payroll growth, but it showed that labor demand had not weakened enough to force the Federal Reserve away from the inflation-focused stance adopted at its June meeting.

Consumer confidence also edged higher in June as lower gasoline prices offset some concern about employment. The details were less uniformly strong than the headline: consumers’ assessment of the labor market deteriorated, and they expected little improvement in coming months. For rates, that combination mattered because it was not weak enough to generate a growth scare. Household sentiment improved while the labor outlook softened only at the margin, leaving the Fed room to wait for the more comprehensive employment report.

The Dallas Fed’s Texas service-sector survey added breadth to the activity signal. Its revenue index increased to 9.8 in June from 5.0, employment jumped to 8.1 from -3.2 and hours worked rose to 3.6 from -0.5. The general business-activity index returned to positive territory at 2.9 from -7.7, while the company-outlook measure improved to 6.1 from -5.4. Firms were also optimistic about the next 6 months, with expected revenue at 33.3 and future general business activity at 17.2.

That improvement came with an uncomfortable cost mix. The input-price index rose to 36.5 from 29.7, wages and benefits increased to 15.3 from 6.2 and selling prices moved up to 7.7 from 5.0. The survey therefore extended the two-sided signal from the previous day’s Texas manufacturing report: regional demand and hiring were firming, but so were pipeline costs. It gave the market a reason to lift real yields without treating the fall in crude as a complete solution to the inflation problem.

Housing offered a counterweight. The FHFA house-price index fell 0.1% in April from March, while the annual increase slowed to 2%. March’s monthly gain was revised up to 0.2% from 0.1%, but the regional distribution showed limited national momentum: monthly changes ranged from a 0.8% decline in the Mountain division to a 1% increase in New England, and annual appreciation ranged from 0.2% in the Pacific region to 4.4% in East North Central. Slower home-price growth reduces one source of shelter and collateral-value pressure, though the release covered April and did not outweigh the more current labor and services evidence.

The curve moved only modestly steeper because the selloff was broad. The 2s10s spread widened 2.2 basis points to 29.1 basis points, and 2s30s increased 2 basis points to 77.8 basis points. Over June, however, the curve remained markedly flatter: the 2-year yield had risen 17 basis points, compared with increases of 2.9 basis points in the 10-year and a 2.1-basis-point decline in the 30-year. The monthly pattern reflected the Fed’s hawkish turn and the collapse in oil, which raised the expected path of short rates while reducing longer-horizon inflation compensation.

Tuesday’s rise in the 10-year real yield to 2.226% also placed it 19.3 basis points above its level a month earlier. The 10-year breakeven, by contrast, was 16.4 basis points lower over the same period. That divergence is central to the June adjustment: investors removed much of the war-related inflation premium but did not return to an easing narrative. Stronger employment evidence, resilient consumption and the capital demands of the AI buildout kept the real discount rate elevated.

Treasury turnover was exceptionally heavy at quarter-end. FINRA recorded $1.864 trillion of par activity, 59.3% more than in the preceding session, across 527,867 trades. Nominal-coupon activity rose 60.9% to $1.388 trillion. Trading in coupons with no more than 2 years remaining increased 68.6% to $338.3 billion, while the sector above 2 and through 3 years more than doubled to $200.2 billion. TIPS activity rose 113.5% to $68.1 billion. Those figures measure two-way transactions rather than investor direction, but they show that the selloff occurred amid extensive quarter-end balance-sheet and portfolio adjustment rather than a thin-market mark.

The front end also absorbed an $80 billion 42-day bill auction. The sale stopped at a 3.655% high rate with a 2.71 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received 69.01% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders took 4.96% and primary dealers were awarded 26.03%. The bills settle July 2 and mature August 13. The result established substantial cash demand across quarter-end and the Independence Day funding window, although the absence of a when-issued reference precludes judging whether the auction tailed or priced through prevailing levels.

Cross-asset trading supported the real-yield interpretation. The Nasdaq 100 and semiconductor index outperformed while the dollar index was almost unchanged at 101.19 and gold was little changed near $4,023. Broad listed bond funds were weaker, led by a 0.57% decline in the investment-grade LQD fund and a 0.39% fall in the emerging-market EMB fund; high-yield funds slipped only marginally. Those price moves were consistent with higher government yields and strong equity risk appetite, rather than a generalized deterioration in corporate solvency.

## Europe’s Inflation Relief Reduces the Urgency to Hike

National inflation reports shifted the European debate from whether the ECB had to follow its June increase with rapid tightening to whether it could wait for evidence of second-round effects. German inflation slowed to 2.4% in June from 2.7%, below the 2.5% median forecast. France’s rate fell to 2% from 2.8%, a much sharper decline than the expected 2.3%, while Italian inflation unexpectedly moderated to 3.1%. Spain’s 3.6% reading remained the principal large-economy exception.

The French details strengthened the case that the improvement was not confined to fuel. Services inflation slowed to 1.8% from 2.1%, and goods prices fell 0.9% from a year earlier after a 0.6% decline in May. Household demand was not collapsing: consumer spending increased 0.5% in May after falling 0.5% in April, exceeding the expected 0.3% gain. Germany’s statistical agency attributed its second consecutive inflation slowdown mainly to more moderate energy costs.

German labor conditions nevertheless remained subdued. Seasonally adjusted unemployment fell by only 1,000 in June. The unadjusted total declined by 15,000 to 2.936 million, but was still 22,000 higher than a year earlier, while the unemployment rate eased to 6.2% from 6.3%. The BA-X labor-demand index was unchanged at 103, and the latest estimate of social-insurance employment was 71,000 lower than a year earlier. Cooling inflation was therefore arriving alongside a labor market that offered little argument for forceful additional restraint.

ECB officials did not declare the energy shock finished, but the coalition for an immediate July increase weakened. Chief Economist Philip Lane focused on how 4 months of higher energy costs may feed into food and services, emphasizing that such indirect effects take time to appear. Dutch Governor Olaf Sleijpen likewise said the full pipeline remained uncertain and identified future wage demands as an important test. Neither committed to another move.

Belgian Governor Pierre Wunsch, normally among the more hawkish members, said another increase might still be needed but that the case was less compelling than it had appeared in June. He favored moving without excessive delay if incoming data justified tightening, while explicitly declining to commit to July. Finland’s Olli Rehn described the energy shock as stagflationary but said he did not see major second-round effects and regarded inflation expectations as anchored.

The more dovish wing put clearer conditions around a pause. Slovenia’s Primoz Dolenc said July could pass without an increase if oil and gas remained subdued, market volatility did not spread and second-round effects failed to emerge. He regarded waiting until September as appropriate on the current evidence, while warning that renewed geopolitical escalation or a significant oil increase could restore the need to act. Latvia’s Martins Kazaks similarly said the urgency of consecutive increases had declined significantly and that the probability of no further tightening was not zero.

That was not a repudiation of June’s move. Kazaks defended it as a response to nearly 4 months of elevated energy prices, while Lane and ECB President Christine Lagarde argued that subsequent developments had not invalidated the decision. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel remained concerned that the energy shock was still passing through the economy. The disagreement concerned the timing and burden of proof for a second step, not whether the ECB should ignore above-target inflation.

The U.K. presented a related but more growth-sensitive problem. Final figures confirmed that real GDP expanded 0.6% in the first quarter after a revised 0.1% increase in the final quarter of 2025. Services grew 0.8%, while production and construction each increased 0.2%. GDP per head rose 0.6% from the preceding quarter and 0.7% from a year earlier, although full-year 2025 growth was revised to 1.3% from 1.4%.

Household finances were weaker than the output headline. Real disposable income per head fell 0.8% after rising 1.2%, and the saving ratio declined to 8.9% from 9.6%. The underlying current-account deficit excluding precious metals narrowed to £15.1 billion, or 1.9% of GDP, from £18.2 billion and 2.4% in the previous quarter. The improvement came from a smaller primary-income deficit, while the trade deficit excluding precious metals widened to £7.7 billion from £2.5 billion.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said the economy’s softness had put the central bank on course for 2 rate cuts before the Iran war interrupted the disinflation path. Oil’s retreat from above $110 to below $80 reduced the danger that the shock would become persistent, even though Bailey expects inflation to rise to about 3.2% later this year from 2.8%. His emphasis was on the 2- to 3-year outlook and the weak economy: tighter financial conditions have bought the BOE time, but the energy shock delayed the anticipated return to its 2% target.

## Japan’s Front End Finds Buyers as the Long End Loses Its Anchor

Japan’s bond market delivered the sharpest curve divergence of the day. A 2-year JGB auction drew a 4.82 bid-to-cover ratio, up from 3.70 at the preceding sale and above the 12-month average of 3.74. The auction tail narrowed to 0.005 from 0.02, and the 2-year yield fell after the result. Investors found the front end attractive after the BOJ raised its policy rate to a 31-year high, especially as the government signaled a preference for cautious additional tightening.

Super-long bonds moved the other way. The 30-year yield climbed 11 basis points to 3.94%, having traded as high as 3.95%, while the 20-year rose 9 basis points to 3.64%. The moves reflected concern that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s fiscal agenda, political pressure on the BOJ and the yen’s decline could leave long-run inflation and government borrowing without a reliable anchor.

The government’s investment roadmap seeks to mobilize more than ¥370 trillion through fiscal 2040 in AI, semiconductors and other strategic sectors. The plan combines public and private resources, but its scale added to concern about an economy whose government debt already exceeds 200% of GDP. At the same time, official policy guidelines were expected to call for appropriate monetary management, language interpreted as encouraging the BOJ to move carefully.

The yen made that combination harder to sustain. It weakened to 162.40 per dollar by the end of June, its lowest level since 1986, despite the BOJ’s latest increase and intervention earlier in the year. Japan spent ¥11.73 trillion between April 28 and May 27 supporting the currency, but the effect faded as the U.S.-Japan rate differential and overseas investment flows continued to favor the dollar. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated that authorities were prepared to act when necessary, without materially strengthening the warning.

A weak yen raises imported energy and raw-material costs, while political resistance to rapid BOJ tightening reduces the most direct monetary response. That tension explains why strong demand for 2-year debt did not support the long end. A cautious BOJ can stabilize policy-sensitive securities, but if the same caution allows currency depreciation and inflation risk to persist, super-long investors require greater compensation.

New BOJ Board Member Ayano Sato added to the perception of a more accommodative future board. At her inaugural press conference, she said an inflationary norm had not become firmly established and declined to disclose how she would vote. She begins participating at the July 30-31 meeting. Takaichi’s previous appointee, Toichiro Asada, was the sole dissenter against the June rate increase, while Sato replaced Junko Nakagawa, who had earlier dissented in favor of tightening. Sato alone does not determine the 9-member board, but the replacement shifts attention toward how future appointments may alter its balance.

Domestic buyers are beginning to respond to the higher long-end yields. Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance plans to purchase more than ¥2 trillion of super-long JGBs in the fiscal year ending March 2027, twice its earlier plan. The insurer regards yields near current levels as attractive and expects the 30-year rate to remain below the 5%-6% range, with the upper end around the mid-4% area for now. That demand provides a potential stabilizer, but it did not prevent Tuesday’s selloff as fiscal and currency concerns intensified.

Asia’s other major activity signal came from China. The official manufacturing PMI increased to 50.3 in June from 50.0, with production at 51.4 and new orders at 51.2. New export orders returned to expansion at 50.1 from 48.6. The non-manufacturing business-activity index edged up to 50.2 from 50.1, and the composite output measure rose to 50.6.

The breadth was weaker than the headline thresholds suggested. Manufacturing employment slipped to 48.5, small-firm PMI fell to 48.2 and construction registered 49.0. Non-manufacturing new orders improved 3 points but remained in contraction at 48.0, while its input-price index fell to 49.7. The data showed output and export demand recovering without a broad improvement in hiring, smaller companies or construction.

Regional bond flows nevertheless benefited from the retreat in oil and efforts to stabilize currencies. Foreign investors bought a net $1.2 billion of Indonesian government bonds through June 26, putting June on course for the largest monthly inflow in 13 months. The 10-year yield stood at 7.12%, down from an early-June peak of 7.47%, after Bank Indonesia delivered a surprise increase and took its cumulative tightening this year to 100 basis points. The rupiah recovered about 2% from its record low.

India received a record 398 billion rupees, or $4.2 billion, of foreign purchases in index-eligible government debt during June after removing taxes on government bonds. The rupee also rebounded from its record low as cheaper oil improved the outlook for an economy heavily dependent on imported energy. European recognition of the Clearing Corp. of India as a permitted central counterparty removed an additional obstacle for banks including Deutsche Bank and BNP Paribas, lowering capital and operational frictions for trading Indian bonds and derivatives.

## Open Credit Markets Still Penalize Refinancing Risk

Emerging-market borrowers took advantage of exceptionally tight valuations before the half-year ended. Sovereigns and companies sold a record $450 billion of dollar- and euro-denominated international bonds in the first 6 months of 2026, 15% more than a year earlier. Mexico, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Poland, Turkey and Brazil each raised more than $10 billion.

The additional yield on emerging-market debt over Treasuries narrowed to 154 basis points in June, the lowest since 2007. EM dollar debt returned 2.1% in the first half, roughly 3 times the Treasury return in the cited indexes. Lower oil, progress toward a U.S.-Iran settlement and longer-run diversification of global savings away from U.S. assets supported demand, allowing established borrowers to issue at historically compressed risk premiums.

Japanese companies also set a financing record abroad. Foreign-currency bond sales reached about $54 billion in the quarter, more than 80% above the year-earlier period and the first quarterly total above $50 billion in data extending to 1999. Mizuho Financial Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group priced almost $10 billion of dollar debt between them, and Panasonic began marketing another dollar issue.

The weak yen increased the amount of domestic funding Japanese issuers could obtain after swapping foreign proceeds, while rising local rates reduced the relative appeal of borrowing at home. Overseas acquisitions supplied a further structural reason to issue in foreign currencies. The record therefore reflected more than opportunistic spread compression: Japanese firms are adapting their funding base to higher domestic yields and a larger international investment footprint.

China moved in the opposite direction by trying to limit expensive offshore refinancing. The National Development and Reform Commission asked selected bankers to avoid underwriting offshore yuan bonds yielding more than 4% and dollar bonds yielding more than 5%, according to people familiar with the matter. Some local-government financing vehicles had their offshore refinancing quotas reduced by 10%-20%, and at least one state-owned enterprise resorted to a costlier short-term bank loan to fill the gap.

The restrictions target a sector with about $117 billion of offshore bonds outstanding. Chinese companies more broadly face approximately $71 billion of offshore maturities during the remainder of 2026, followed by a maturity peak above $130 billion in 2027. Lower-cost discipline may reduce the accumulation of high-coupon debt, but it can also force weaker issuers toward shorter bank funding or leave a larger refinancing gap when offshore market yields exceed the regulatory thresholds.

Sable Offshore showed the other side of an otherwise receptive leveraged-finance market. The company’s shares fell as much as 55% after it announced plans to raise $400 million through stock and convertible-note offerings to repay an Exxon Mobil loan. A proposed term loan initially sized at $1 billion was reduced for a second time to $675 million after demand remained limited even at a 15% fixed interest rate and an issue price of 97 cents on the dollar.

The 2½-year loan also required partial amortization, while proposed convertible bonds offered a coupon as high as 6.5% and a 30%-35% conversion premium. Sable had paid Exxon $30 million to extend a June 26 maturity, with the deadline subsequently expected to run through July 31. Litigation surrounding the restart of its California offshore operations left investors assessing both near-term repayment pressure and the durability of the underlying business. The difficulty was issuer-specific: other leveraged borrowers were tightening pricing and accelerating transaction deadlines.

Ethiopia’s restructuring produced a different form of creditor dispute. A committee representing about 45% of holders of its defaulted 2024 notes confirmed a tentative agreement on key terms, helping the bonds reach 109.17 cents, near a 6-month high. The group nevertheless accused the IMF of mishandling the process and argued that its role as both senior creditor and assessor of debt-relief needs created a conflict. The IMF said the agreement was consistent with restoring debt sustainability and defended the consistency and transparency of its framework. The prospective settlement advanced, but the dispute showed that price recovery need not imply confidence in the sovereign-restructuring process.

Private credit was also drawing capital toward prospective stress. Len Tannenbaum was seeking family-office backing for a new fund, with his own family prepared to provide as much as $50 million and a first close targeted for early October. He expects outflows from private-credit vehicles to improve spreads and covenants, particularly in the lower middle market, and sees smaller software borrowers facing refinancing difficulty over the next year. The proposed vehicle had not filed its documentation and had not decided whether an eventual business development company would be public or private.

The IMF’s Tobias Adrian identified a related vulnerability in large technology borrowers. He argued that debt financing deserves more concern than elevated equity valuations because hyperscalers are funding physical assets and chips that may become obsolete faster than medium- or long-term debt matures. Continued profitability can sustain that structure, but an earnings disappointment would expose the mismatch. The warning gained relevance as semiconductor shares completed their strongest quarter while firms and governments committed vast additional sums to AI infrastructure.

## Policy Paths Diverge Across Emerging Markets

Colombia delivered the day’s largest realized policy move, raising its benchmark rate by 75 basis points to 12%. It was the first increase since March and exceeded the forecast of most of the 26 analysts surveyed. Four of the 7 board members supported the move, while one favored no change and 2 preferred a 50-basis-point reduction, revealing a deeply divided reaction function despite the large headline increase.

The bank cited above-target inflation expectations and a tight labor market. Annual inflation accelerated to 5.8% in May, the fastest in almost 2 years, and economists surveyed by the central bank expect it to reach about 6.5% at year-end, against a 3% target with a tolerance band of 1 percentage point. A wide fiscal deficit and a record minimum-wage increase added to the pressure.

Institutional conditions had also changed. A court suspended the requirement that the finance minister attend policy meetings, removing a mechanism that had allowed the government to threaten a boycott and block decisions. Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella’s presidential-election victory over Iván Cepeda reduced concern that political pressure on the central bank would continue. Bonds and the currency had rallied after the election, giving policymakers more room to reassert the inflation mandate.

South Africa’s next move remained prospective but became more hawkish. Average inflation expectations 2 years ahead rose to 3.9% from 3.6%, the first increase in more than a year and above the central bank’s 3% target. Goldman Sachs expects a unanimous 25-basis-point increase at the July 23 meeting after the previous move lifted the policy rate to 7%; forward-rate agreements assigned an 88% probability to another quarter-point step.

The South African survey was conducted from May 18 through June 4, before the 60-day U.S.-Iran ceasefire reopened Hormuz and drove energy prices lower. That timing limits how much the result captures the subsequent oil reversal. Goldman expects cheaper fuel to reduce inflation in coming months and potentially allow the bank to pause after July before resuming cuts in the second quarter of 2027. The immediate tightening case rests on preventing expectations from becoming entrenched, not on assuming the energy shock will continue at its earlier intensity.

Poland supplied the opposite outcome. Inflation slowed for a third month to 2.5% in June from 3.1%, below the 2.7% median forecast. The zloty weakened 0.3% against the euro, while benchmark government bonds rallied and the 10-year yield fell to its lowest since early March. Local economists said the probability of another increase had fallen close to zero, with derivatives assigning greater odds to eventual easing.

The Polish result demonstrated how lower oil was separating regional policy paths. The inflation effect of the Middle East conflict proved less severe than feared, and June marked a fourth consecutive undershoot relative to forecasts. The central bank is still likely to hold over the next several meetings, but weaker growth or core inflation could open the way to reductions. Fertilizer costs remain a longer-term risk to the food-price outlook.

New Zealand faced a more gradual normalization debate. The IMF said the Reserve Bank should withdraw accommodation and move its 2.25% policy rate toward a neutral level centered around 3% by the end of 2026. The recommendation did not specify whether tightening should begin at the next meeting or in September. It made the path conditional on core inflation, medium-term expectations and the recovery, which the IMF expects to resume in the second half after a second-quarter contraction.

Chile’s curve illustrated how improving inflation can coexist with worsening fiscal duration risk. One-year breakeven inflation fell more than 100 basis points over the month to 2.19%, below the central bank’s 3% target, and more than 40% of surveyed analysts and traders expected peso yields to decline in July. Market pricing put the policy rate at 4.38% in a year, compared with 4.5% currently.

Long-term Chilean yields rose, however, after the government abandoned its plan to balance the structural budget by 2030 and instead targeted a deficit equal to 1.5% of GDP by the end of its term. It requested authority to sell an additional $6.2 billion of bonds during 2026. Lower inflation and economic slack supported shorter maturities, while prospective supply and a weaker fiscal anchor raised the term premium farther out the curve.

## Forward Market Significance

Euro-area flash inflation at 11:00 CEST on July 1 is the first major test. The May headline rate was 3.2%, with the measure excluding energy at 2.4%. The large national releases point toward moderation, but their dispersion leaves the ECB focused on whether services, food and wages show the delayed pass-through described by Lane and Sleijpen. A broad slowdown would strengthen the case for pausing in July; persistence beneath the energy component would preserve the option of another increase.

The U.S. calendar then delivers ADP employment at 08:15 ET, final manufacturing PMI at 09:45 and ISM manufacturing with construction spending at 10:00. The previous ISM report showed manufacturing at 54.0, prices at 82.1 and employment at 48.6. Orders, hiring and prices will indicate whether the resilient JOLTS and Texas services readings describe a national reacceleration or a narrower set of firm regional observations.

Treasury will auction $72 billion of 17-week bills at 11:30 ET on July 1 for July 7 settlement and November 3 maturity. The sale follows firm absorption of the 42-day bill but shifts the cash date beyond quarter-end. It will test whether demand remains strong once the immediate reporting-date pressures have passed and before the shortened July 2 session.

The holiday-advanced U.S. employment report and initial jobless claims arrive at 08:30 ET on July 2. May payrolls rose 172,000, unemployment was 4.3% and average hourly earnings increased 0.3% from the month before and 3.4% from a year earlier. The June composition—especially wages and whether hiring broadens beyond defensive sectors—will be the most important near-term test of the Fed tightening bias embedded in the rise in real yields.

May factory orders follow at 10:00 ET, after advance durable-goods orders fell 4.5%. Treasury then sells $85 billion each of 4- and 8-week bills at 11:30 for July 7 settlement. The SIFMA-recommended fixed-income close is 14:00 ET, concentrating payrolls, factory data, bill supply and position adjustment into a shortened trading window. U.S. fixed-income markets are closed July 3, with no New York Fed reference-rate publication or Desk operations that day.

Japan’s roughly ¥2.6 trillion 10-year JGB auction on July 2 will test whether the strong front-end demand seen at the 2-year sale extends into core duration. The result will arrive against a 40-year low in the yen, a more accommodative-looking BOJ board and a sharp super-long selloff. The approximately ¥600 billion 30-year auction on July 7 is the more direct test of whether insurers’ increased purchase plans can stabilize the part of the curve most exposed to fiscal expansion and long-run inflation uncertainty.

Energy remains the common condition across those policy tests. WTI ended June near $69.50 after falling more than 20% during the month, but Qatar described the Doha negotiations as indirect and played down the prospect of an immediate breakthrough. Continued Hormuz traffic and a durable ceasefire would keep headline inflation relief intact. Renewed attacks, restrictions on maritime passage or a failure to formalize the settlement would return energy inflation and long-end term premium to the center of global rates trading.

Europe moved toward a less urgent tightening debate, Japan’s curve split sharply between the front and long ends, and open credit markets imposed steep penalties on borrowers with urgent refinancing or uncertain cash generation.

Germany’s subdued labor market reinforced the case for patience. In the U.K., stronger Q1 output masked weaker household finances, while cheaper oil gave the BOE more time to judge whether inflation will persist.

Planned insurer purchases may stabilize super-long debt. Elsewhere, China’s PMI improved unevenly, while cheaper oil and currency stabilization supported bond inflows into Indonesia and India.

section_summaries.summary: Emerging-market international issuance reached a first-half record of $450 billion, and Japanese companies set a quarterly foreign-currency issuance record. That broad access did not extend evenly: China discouraged costly offshore borrowing by indebted local-government financing vehicles, while Sable Offshore struggled to place a reduced $675 million loan even at a 15% rate. Credit remained available, but refinancing urgency and uncertain cash generation commanded severe terms.

section_summaries.market_read: Lower oil eased inflation pressure unevenly, leaving domestic expectations, fiscal credibility and labor conditions to drive policy divergence.
section_summaries.next_check: South Africa’s July 23 decision will test whether higher expectations outweigh the subsequent oil reversal.
section_summaries.section_title: Policy Paths Diverge Across Emerging Markets
section_summaries.summary: Colombia raised its policy rate 75 basis points to 12% as inflation and fiscal risks outweighed a divided board. South Africa faced a prospective July increase after inflation expectations rose, while Poland’s inflation slowdown reduced the likelihood of further tightening. The IMF urged New Zealand toward neutral by year-end, and Chile combined improving short-term inflation pricing with higher long-end yields after weakening its fiscal target and seeking more bond issuance.

Euro-area flash inflation will test whether national disinflation extends beyond energy, while U.S. payrolls and wages will determine whether resilient labor demand validates the rise in real yields. Japan’s 10- and 30-year auctions will show whether demand extends beyond the front end. Continued Hormuz traffic and a durable ceasefire remain necessary to preserve the energy relief shaping these policy tests.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury yields jump as resilient U.S. demand lifts real rates
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury yields rose across the curve on June 30, reversing much of the preceding week’s duration rally. The 2-year yield increased 6.8 basis points to 4.175%, the 5-year climbed 8.4 basis points to 4.227%, the 10-year rose 9 basis points to 4.466% and the 30-year advanced 8.8 basis points to 4.953%.

The move was predominantly real-rate driven: the 10-year real yield increased 7.8 basis points to 2.226%, while the 10-year breakeven rose only 1.2 basis points to 2.24%. Job openings reached 7.59 million, consumer confidence edged higher and Texas services reported faster revenue and employment growth alongside stronger input and wage costs. Softer house prices and weaker consumer views of the labor market qualified the signal without creating a growth scare.

Oil’s decline restrained inflation compensation, while a technology-led equity rally and lower volatility reinforced risk appetite and reduced demand for government bonds. Europe’s softer inflation readings reduced the urgency for another immediate ECB increase. Japan diverged as strong demand at a 2-year auction contrasted with an 11-basis-point rise in the 30-year yield amid yen weakness, fiscal expansion and pressure for cautious BOJ tightening.

Credit remained broadly available but selective. Record emerging-market and Japanese foreign-currency issuance contrasted with Sable Offshore’s difficulty placing a 15% loan and China’s effort to curb expensive offshore refinancing by heavily indebted local-government financing vehicles.
